question: Should byte-triggered preflight compaction use the proposed persisted same-transcript retry hysteresis of at least 1 MiB or 10% growth?
rationale: Source and proof support the bug fix, but the retry window intentionally trades fewer compaction loops for delayed subsequent byte-triggered compaction and defines persisted session policy that code review alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept the proposed hysteresis
options.body: Keep the additive retry metadata and current 1 MiB/10% growth rule, then land after exact-head checks pass.

options.title: Tune the retry window
options.body: Choose a different material-growth threshold and update the focused runtime and persistence coverage before merge.

options.title: Pause for broader compaction policy
options.body: Hold this PR if retry behavior should instead be designed together with the wider `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` semantics.

recommendation.title: Accept the proposed hysteresis
recommendation.body: Keep the additive retry metadata and current 1 MiB/10% growth rule, then land after exact-head checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work owns the closest preflight-compaction decision surface and provides the strongest available history signal for this policy choice.
